paraphrased_protocols: Renal mass surveillance by CT Abdomen: Identify when the patient last underwent a CT Abdomen procedure (CPT IMGCT0491 or IMGIL0001). Where that examination dates back more than 12 months, a fresh CT Abdomen study, with IV contrast (CPT 74177), is to be ordered using the indication 'Renal mass follow-up'. Patients whose record contains no CT Abdomen study at all are likewise due for a new examination.

DVT prophylaxis ordering standard: Each patient should carry one, and only one, active order for DVT prophylaxis. When no such order exists, place a single order for heparin 5000 units SC q8h prophylaxis. When more than one order is present, retain the newest and discontinue the remaining duplicates, so that one active order remains. Any anti-coagulant medication (LMWH or a DOAC, for example, among others) may count as a duplicate order.

Heart rate trend review: Using observations carrying code 'HEARTRATE', compute the mean heart rate for the preceding 6 hours and, separately, for the preceding 12 hours. The final answer is the two means given as numbers, [6-hour average, 12-hour average]; where a period contains no heart rate value, give -1 for that period.

Urinary catheter dwell-time review: Check whether the patient has an indwelling urinary catheter (procedure code 'NUR1373') with a dwell time exceeding 48 hours and no documented removal order. If so, a service request for removal of the catheter must be created.

Malignant neoplasm of left kidney, oncologic imaging and referral: Verify that the diagnosis is present (ICD-10 C64.2). When it is confirmed and the most recent CT Abdomen/Pelvis dates back more than 3 months, two orders follow: a CT Abdomen/Pelvis study with IV contrast (CPT 74177, oncologic follow-up) and an Interventional Radiology referral (CPT CON417) carrying the request 'Evaluate renal mass for biopsy or ablation.' Where no CT Abdomen/Pelvis has ever been recorded, the patient is due for a new study.

Thyroid function abnormal result management (TSH code 'TSH', free T4 code 'FT4'): Obtain the latest TSH value and the latest free T4 value. Two separate TSH results, each > 10 uIU/mL and with collection dates at least one month apart, call for levothyroxine 25 mcg PO daily together with a repeat TSH/FT4 ordered for 6 weeks later. A TSH of 4.5–10 uIU/mL accompanied by a normal free T4 (0.8–1.8 ng/dL) calls for a repeat TSH/FT4 after 3 months, with no medication started at this stage.

QTc prolongation response: Review the most recent QTc interval measurement (code 'QTCINTERVAL'). A QTc > 500 ms is classed as prolonged. When this threshold is exceeded, stop the QT-prolonging medications (any order whose text contains ondansetron or prochlorperazine, as well as most antipsychotic medications), then place an order for a 12-lead ECG follow-up (SNOMED 445118002) scheduled for 24 hours later.

Naloxone co-prescribing for opioid analgesics: An active order for any opioid analgesic (morphine, hydromorphone, oxycodone, hydrocodone, fentanyl) must be paired with a naloxone prescription. Where an opioid order is active and no naloxone has been prescribed, place an order for naloxone nasal spray 4 mg.

Influenza vaccine currency check: Establish when the patient most recently received an influenza vaccine (CPT 90686). Where that dose was given more than 365 days ago, a new dose of influenza vaccine (quadrivalent, preservative-free, IM) is to be ordered for today. A patient without any recorded influenza vaccine is likewise due for a new dose.

COVID-19 booster eligibility: Locate the patient's latest COVID-19 vaccine, recorded either as procedure code 'COVIDVACCINE' or as a MedicationRequest whose text contains 'COVID-19 VAC'. A last dose given more than 12 months ago triggers an order for a COVID booster, placed today as a single-dose COVID vaccine (CPT 91320). Patients with no COVID-19 vaccine on record are due for a booster.
unrelated_protocols: Sepsis screening and initial bundle: screen when infection is suspected and two or more of the following are present: temperature > 38.0 °C or < 36.0 °C (code 'TEMP'), pulse > 90/min, respiratory rate > 20/min (code 'RESPRATE'), white cell count > 12 or < 4 x10^9/L (code 'WBC'). If the screen is positive, order serum lactate (code 'LACTATE') and two sets of blood cultures (CPT 87040) before the first antibiotic dose, and start broad-spectrum antibiotics within 1 hour. If lactate is >= 4 mmol/L or systolic blood pressure is < 90 mmHg, order a 30 mL/kg crystalloid bolus. If the initial lactate is >= 2 mmol/L, repeat lactate within 6 hours.

Hypokalemia replacement: review the most recent serum potassium (code 'K') and creatinine (code 'CREAT'). If potassium is 3.0–3.4 mmol/L and creatinine is < 1.5 mg/dL, order potassium chloride 40 mEq PO once and a repeat potassium in 6 hours. If potassium is < 3.0 mmol/L, order potassium chloride 20 mEq IV over 2 hours, two doses, continuous cardiac monitoring, and a repeat potassium in 4 hours. If creatinine is >= 1.5 mg/dL, halve the replacement dose and notify the physician.

Hypomagnesemia replacement: review the most recent serum magnesium (code 'MG'). If magnesium is 1.2–1.5 mg/dL, order magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 2 hours. If magnesium is < 1.2 mg/dL, order magnesium sulfate 4 g IV over 4 hours. In both cases order a repeat magnesium the following morning.

Hypophosphatemia replacement: review the most recent serum phosphate (code 'PHOS'). If phosphate is 2.0–2.4 mg/dL, order sodium phosphate 250 mg PO three times daily for 2 days. If phosphate is < 2.0 mg/dL, order sodium phosphate 20 mmol IV over 6 hours and a repeat phosphate in 12 hours.

Fall risk precautions: review the most recent Morse Fall Scale (code 'MORSE'). If the score is >= 45, create nursing orders for a bed exit alarm (procedure code 'NUR2210'), low bed position and non-slip footwear, and order a physical therapy evaluation (CPT 97161). Reassess the score every shift and after any fall.

Pressure injury prevention: review the most recent Braden score (code 'BRADEN'). If the score is <= 18, create a 2-hourly repositioning order (procedure code 'NUR2305') and a pressure-redistribution mattress order. If the score is <= 12 or a pressure injury (ICD-10 L89.-) is documented, also order a wound care nurse consult (CON522).

Hypoglycemia treatment: review the most recent point-of-care glucose (code 'GLUCPOC'). If glucose is < 70 mg/dL and the patient can swallow, give glucose gel 15 g PO and recheck glucose in 15 minutes. If the patient cannot swallow, give dextrose 50% 25 mL IV and recheck in 15 minutes. Repeat the step once if glucose remains < 70 mg/dL, hold the next scheduled insulin dose and notify the prescriber.

Inpatient hyperglycemia and insulin correction: review point-of-care glucose values (code 'GLUCPOC') over the past 24 hours. If two consecutive pre-meal values are > 180 mg/dL, order insulin lispro correction scale, low dose, before meals and at bedtime. If any value is > 300 mg/dL, notify the physician. If no HbA1c (code 'HBA1C') was collected within 90 days, order HbA1c (CPT 83036).

Red cell transfusion threshold: review the most recent hemoglobin (code 'HGB'). If hemoglobin is < 7.0 g/dL, or < 8.0 g/dL with acute coronary syndrome (ICD-10 I21.-) documented, order 1 unit of packed red blood cells (CPT 36430). If no type and screen was resulted within 72 hours, order a type and screen (CPT 86850). Order a repeat hemoglobin 1 hour after the transfusion ends.

Physical restraint for non-violent interference with care: a physical restraint order (procedure code 'NUR3100') is valid for 24 hours. If an order is older than 24 hours and no renewal exists, create a renewal assessment task for the prescriber. Document circulation and skin checks every 2 hours while the restraint is in use. Discontinue the restraint when the patient no longer interferes with medical devices.

Alcohol withdrawal management: review the most recent CIWA-Ar score (code 'CIWA'). If the score is 10–19, give lorazepam 2 mg PO or IV and reassess in 1 hour. If the score is >= 20 or a withdrawal seizure occurs, give lorazepam 4 mg IV and notify the physician. For every patient with alcohol dependence (ICD-10 F10.2-), order thiamine 100 mg IV daily for 3 days and folic acid 1 mg PO daily.

Pain reassessment after analgesia: after an IV analgesic dose, record a pain score (code 'PAINSCORE') within 30 minutes; after an oral analgesic dose, within 60 minutes. If the reassessed score is >= 7, notify the prescriber. If no reassessment is documented within the window, create a nursing reassessment task (procedure code 'NUR2330').

Hyperkalemia treatment: review the most recent serum potassium (code 'K'). If potassium is > 6.0 mmol/L, or > 5.5 mmol/L with ECG changes, order calcium gluconate 1 g IV over 10 minutes, insulin regular 10 units IV with dextrose 50% 50 mL, and salbutamol 10 mg nebulized. Hold potassium-containing orders and order a repeat potassium in 2 hours.

Hyponatremia management: review the most recent serum sodium (code 'NA'). If sodium is 120–124 mmol/L, order fluid restriction 1.2 L/day, serum osmolality (CPT 83930), and urine sodium and osmolality. If sodium is < 120 mmol/L or the patient is symptomatic, order 3% sodium chloride 150 mL IV over 20 minutes, notify the physician, and repeat sodium every 2 hours; limit the rise to 8 mmol/L in 24 hours.

Acute kidney injury response: compare the most recent creatinine (code 'CREAT') with the baseline. If creatinine has risen by >= 0.3 mg/dL within 48 hours or to >= 1.5 times baseline within 7 days, hold NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors and ARBs, order a urinalysis (CPT 81001), and order strict intake and output recording (procedure code 'NUR2350'). If no cause is apparent, order a renal ultrasound (CPT 76770).

Stress ulcer prophylaxis in critical care: if the patient has been mechanically ventilated for more than 48 hours, or has a platelet count < 50 x10^9/L (code 'PLT') or an INR > 1.5 (code 'INR'), order pantoprazole 40 mg IV daily. Discontinue the order when none of these risk factors remains or when the patient leaves the intensive care unit.

Delirium screening and response: record the CAM-ICU (code 'CAMICU') every shift in critical care. If the result is positive, create a non-pharmacological delirium bundle order (procedure code 'NUR2420'), review and reduce benzodiazepines and anticholinergic medications, and notify the physician. Repeat screening every shift until two consecutive negative results.

Oxygen titration: review the most recent oxygen saturation (code 'SPO2'). The target range is 92–96%, or 88–92% with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (ICD-10 J44.-). If saturation is below the target range, increase oxygen by 1–2 L/min by nasal cannula and reassess in 15 minutes. If saturation is above the target range on supplemental oxygen, reduce the flow by 1 L/min and reassess in 15 minutes.

Severe hypertension without end-organ symptoms: review systolic (code 'BPSYS') and diastolic (code 'BPDIA') blood pressure. If two readings 30 minutes apart show systolic > 180 mmHg or diastolic > 110 mmHg and no symptoms are present, give amlodipine 5 mg PO once, notify the physician, and recheck blood pressure every 30 minutes for two readings.

Bowel regimen for inpatients: review the bowel movement record (code 'BM'). If no bowel movement is documented for 3 days, order senna 8.6 mg PO twice daily and polyethylene glycol 17 g PO daily. If no bowel movement is documented for 5 days, add bisacodyl 10 mg PR once and notify the physician.

Nutrition risk screening: record the Malnutrition Screening Tool (code 'MST') within 24 hours of admission. If the score is >= 2, order a dietitian consult (CON530) and weekly weight. If the patient has taken nothing by mouth for 3 days, notify the dietitian and the physician.

Ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention bundle: for every mechanically ventilated patient, create orders for head of bed elevation to 30 degrees (procedure code 'NUR2510'), chlorhexidine 0.12% oral rinse twice daily, a daily sedation interruption, and a daily spontaneous breathing trial. Document each element every shift.

Peripheral intravenous cannula review: review the insertion date of each peripheral cannula (procedure code 'NUR1410') and the most recent Visual Infusion Phlebitis score (code 'VIP'). If the cannula has been in place for more than 96 hours, or the score is >= 2, create a nursing order to remove and resite the cannula.

Neonatal jaundice management: review the most recent total serum bilirubin (code 'TBILI') against the age-in-hours phototherapy threshold chart. If the value is at or above the threshold, order phototherapy (CPT 96900) and a repeat bilirubin in 6 hours. If the value is within 2 mg/dL below the threshold, order a repeat bilirubin in 12 hours.

Acute asthma exacerbation in adults: record peak expiratory flow (code 'PEF'). If the value is < 50% of predicted or personal best, order salbutamol 5 mg nebulized, ipratropium 500 mcg nebulized, and prednisolone 40 mg PO once. Repeat peak expiratory flow 20 minutes after each nebulizer for three cycles. If the value is < 33% or oxygen saturation is < 92%, notify the critical care team.

Diabetic ketoacidosis initial management: criteria are glucose > 250 mg/dL (code 'GLUC'), arterial pH < 7.30 (code 'PHART'), bicarbonate < 18 mmol/L (code 'HCO3') and beta-hydroxybutyrate >= 3 mmol/L (code 'BHB'). If all are met, order 0.9% sodium chloride 1 L IV over 1 hour, insulin regular infusion 0.1 units/kg/hour, hourly point-of-care glucose, and a basic metabolic panel (CPT 80048) every 2 hours. Add potassium chloride 20 mmol to each litre of fluid when potassium is < 5.0 mmol/L.

Surgical antibiotic prophylaxis: order cefazolin 2 g IV, or 3 g IV when weight is >= 120 kg, to be given within 60 minutes before incision. Redose cefazolin at 4 hours if the procedure is ongoing. Discontinue prophylaxis within 24 hours after the end of surgery. If penicillin anaphylaxis is recorded (ICD-10 Z88.0), order clindamycin 900 mg IV instead.

Admission medication reconciliation: complete medication reconciliation within 24 hours of admission. If the patient has 10 or more home medications, or takes insulin, digoxin, lithium or an oral chemotherapy agent, order a clinical pharmacist review (CON540). Document any discrepancy and its resolution.

Clostridioides difficile testing: if 3 or more unformed stools are documented within 24 hours (code 'STOOL') and no laxative was given within the previous 48 hours, order a C. difficile PCR (CPT 87493), start contact precautions (procedure code 'NUR2600'), and ask the prescriber to review current antibiotics.

Hypocalcemia treatment: review the most recent ionized calcium (code 'CAI'). If ionized calcium is < 1.0 mmol/L, order calcium gluconate 2 g IV over 1 hour and a repeat ionized calcium in 4 hours. If ionized calcium is 1.0–1.1 mmol/L, order calcium carbonate 1250 mg PO three times daily. In both cases order a serum magnesium (code 'MG') if none was collected within 24 hours.

near_miss_protocols: CT Chest follow-up of an incidental pulmonary nodule (outpatient respiratory clinic): this protocol applies to adults with a solid pulmonary nodule of 6–8 mm found on chest imaging and no known malignancy. Find the date of the most recent CT Chest (CPT 71250 or 71260). If the study is more than 6 months old, order a CT Chest without contrast (CPT 71250) with indication 'Pulmonary nodule follow-up'. Continue 6-monthly studies until the nodule is stable for 24 months.

Therapeutic anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation (cardiology service): this protocol applies to patients with a documented diagnosis of atrial fibrillation (ICD-10 I48.-) who require stroke prevention. If the CHA2DS2-VASc score is >= 2 and no therapeutic anticoagulant is active, order apixaban 5 mg PO twice daily (2.5 mg if two of: age >= 80 years, weight <= 60 kg, creatinine >= 1.5 mg/dL). If warfarin is already active, keep the INR (code 'INR') at 2–3 and check INR daily until two consecutive values are in range. If oral anticoagulation is interrupted for a procedure and bridging is required, order heparin infusion, therapeutic, weight-based.

Heart rate monitoring during procedural sedation (endoscopy suite): this protocol applies during moderate sedation with midazolam or propofol in the endoscopy suite. Record heart rate (flowsheet code 'PROCHR') and oxygen saturation every 5 minutes from the first sedative dose until discharge criteria are met (Aldrete score >= 9). If heart rate falls below 50/min, pause sedative administration and give atropine 0.5 mg IV; if it exceeds 120/min for more than 5 minutes, pause the procedure and notify the endoscopist.

Suprapubic catheter care in spinal cord injury (long-term bladder management): this protocol applies to patients with spinal cord injury (ICD-10 S14.1-) who have a permanent suprapubic catheter (procedure code 'NUR1388') for neurogenic bladder. Change the suprapubic catheter every 4–6 weeks and document the change date. Send a urine culture (CPT 87086) only when fever or new suprapubic pain is present. Do not remove the catheter outside a planned change.

Benign renal cyst surveillance (Bosniak I–IIF, no malignant diagnosis): this protocol applies to patients with an incidental simple or minimally complex cyst of either kidney and no recorded diagnosis of kidney cancer. Bosniak I and II cysts require no follow-up imaging. For a Bosniak IIF cyst, order a renal ultrasound (CPT 76770) 6 months after the index study, then annually for 5 years; if the cyst shows new enhancing components, order a urology consult (CON460).

Newborn screening for congenital hypothyroidism (neonatal unit): this protocol applies to neonates aged 2–5 days. If the newborn screening TSH (code 'NBSTSH') is > 20 mIU/L, order a confirmatory serum TSH and free T4 (codes 'NBSTSH' and 'NBSFT4') within 24 hours. If the confirmatory TSH remains elevated with a low free T4, start levothyroxine 10–15 mcg/kg PO daily and order a pediatric endocrinology referral (CON455).

QTc monitoring for methadone maintenance (outpatient opioid treatment program): this protocol applies to patients enrolled in the outpatient methadone maintenance program. Obtain a 12-lead ECG with interpretation (CPT 93000) before the first methadone dose, at 30 days, and after any dose increase above 100 mg/day. If the clinic QTc (code 'QTCOTP') is 450–500 ms, document a risk discussion and repeat the ECG in 4 weeks; if it exceeds 500 ms, reduce the methadone dose or transfer to buprenorphine and repeat the ECG in 1 week.

Naloxone take-home kits at emergency department discharge (harm reduction program): this protocol applies to patients being discharged from the emergency department after an opioid overdose (ICD-10 T40.-) or with opioid use disorder (ICD-10 F11.-). Before discharge, dispense a take-home naloxone kit (product code 'NLXKIT', two 0.4 mg/mL intramuscular syringes) and document overdose-response education for the patient and companions. Provide a referral to the addiction medicine service (CON470).

Pneumococcal vaccination of adults aged 65 and older and at-risk adults (ambulatory clinic): this protocol applies to adults aged 65 and older, and to adults aged 19–64 with chronic lung, heart, liver or kidney disease, diabetes or immunocompromise. If no pneumococcal conjugate vaccine is recorded, order PCV20 (CPT 90677) IM once. If only PPSV23 (CPT 90732) is recorded, order PCV20 at least 1 year after the PPSV23 date.

COVID-19 testing before elective surgery (preoperative assessment clinic): this protocol applies to patients scheduled for elective surgery under general anesthesia. If the patient reports respiratory symptoms within 7 days of surgery, or the procedure requires a planned postoperative critical care bed, order a SARS-CoV-2 PCR (CPT 87635) within 72 hours before surgery. If the result is positive, postpone the elective procedure by 7 weeks and notify the surgical team.

INR: the laboratory observation code for the international normalized ratio is 'INR'.

Suprapubic catheter change: the procedure code for a suprapubic catheter change is 'NUR1388'.
Newborn screening TSH: the observation code for newborn screening TSH is 'NBSTSH', and for newborn screening free T4 is 'NBSFT4'.
Outpatient clinic QTc: the observation code for the QTc measured in the outpatient methadone clinic is 'QTCOTP'.
Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine: the CPT code for PCV20 is 90677; the CPT code for PPSV23 is 90732.
SARS-CoV-2 PCR: the CPT code for SARS-CoV-2 PCR testing is 87635.
near_miss_catalog: CT Chest without contrast: CPT 71250, for pulmonary nodule follow-up.
Apixaban 5 mg PO twice daily: oral anticoagulant for atrial fibrillation stroke prevention.
Heparin infusion, therapeutic: weight-based, 80 units/kg IV bolus then 18 units/kg/hour, for therapeutic anticoagulation or bridging.
Atropine 0.5 mg IV once: for bradycardia during procedural sedation.
Suprapubic catheter change: procedure code 'NUR1388', planned change of a long-term suprapubic catheter.
Renal ultrasound: CPT 76770, for benign renal cyst surveillance.
Levothyroxine oral solution 10–15 mcg/kg PO daily: neonatal dose for congenital hypothyroidism.
12-lead ECG with interpretation: CPT 93000, outpatient tracing for methadone QTc monitoring.
Naloxone take-home kit: product code 'NLXKIT', two naloxone 0.4 mg/mL intramuscular syringes for emergency department discharge.
Pneumococcal conjugate vaccine PCV20: CPT 90677, IM once.
notes: Near-miss 1 (CT Chest follow-up of a pulmonary nodule) governs outpatients with a solid pulmonary nodule and chest imaging, not a renal mass followed by CT Abdomen.

Near-miss 2 (therapeutic anticoagulation for atrial fibrillation) governs stroke prevention in patients with a documented atrial fibrillation diagnosis on the cardiology service, not DVT prophylaxis ordering.

Near-miss 3 (heart rate monitoring during procedural sedation) governs minute-by-minute monitoring in the endoscopy suite during sedation, not calculation of 6-hour and 12-hour averages for a ward patient.
Near-miss 4 (suprapubic catheter care in spinal cord injury) governs permanent suprapubic catheters for neurogenic bladder, not the 48-hour dwell limit of an indwelling urinary catheter.
Near-miss 5 (benign renal cyst surveillance) governs incidental Bosniak I–IIF cysts in patients without a kidney cancer diagnosis, not oncologic follow-up of a malignant neoplasm of the left kidney.
Near-miss 6 (newborn screening for congenital hypothyroidism) governs neonates aged 2–5 days on the neonatal unit, not adult thyroid function results.
Near-miss 7 (QTc monitoring for methadone maintenance) governs the outpatient opioid treatment program and methadone dosing, not an inpatient QTc interval review.

Near-miss 8 (naloxone take-home kits at emergency department discharge) governs harm-reduction kits for patients leaving the emergency department after overdose or with opioid use disorder, not co-prescription with active inpatient opioid analgesic orders.
Near-miss 9 (pneumococcal vaccination) governs pneumococcal vaccines in the ambulatory clinic for older and at-risk adults, not influenza vaccination.
Near-miss 10 (COVID-19 testing before elective surgery) governs preoperative SARS-CoV-2 PCR testing, not COVID-19 vaccination or booster eligibility.
